title: The coverage audit silently skips every forwardRef component
description:
The design-system coverage audit has never checked 38 of the 69+ exports it claims to.

`yarn coverage:design-system` reports "69/69 exports in the gallery" on every run, and that line has been quoted as evidence in this epic's gate and in several issue closures. It is a half-truth.

scripts/design-system/check-coverage.mjs, componentExports():

  .filter(([name, value]) => /^[A-Z]/.test(name) && typeof value === 'function')

`forwardRef()` returns an object carrying `$$typeof`, not a function. So every component built with it is skipped silently - it is neither counted nor reported as missing.

Measured against the real barrel:

  counted by the audit          69
  invisible to the audit        38
  Eyebrow counted?              false
  SectionLabel counted?         false

The invisible 38 are the most-used primitives in the system: AppFrame, ContentContainer, Section, Stack, Grid, ProseMeasure, Surface, Text, and on. A `forwardRef` component can be exported with no gallery entry at all and the audit still prints a clean 69/69.

Found while adding `SectionLabel`: it was exported, registered in the gallery, and the count never moved off 69 either way - which is what gave it away.

The fix is small - accept objects whose `$$typeof` is a React element type alongside functions - but it is not a one-liner in effect: turning it on will very likely reveal exports with no gallery entry, and each of those is a real gap the audit was built to catch. Worth doing deliberately rather than as a drive-by.
close_reason: Closed

title: The app shell wraps every page and uses none of the design system
description:
Every page was migrated. The frame around them was not.

src/app/layouts/ - AppLayout, Navbar, Footer, NavLinkButton, UserMenu - imports the design system exactly ZERO times. It is raw Chakra plus the pre-v2 animation components:

  AppLayout      Box, Flex from @chakra-ui/react
  Navbar         Chakra primitives + AnimatedPrimaryButton, Glassmorphism,
                 MotionWrapper, BrandLogo from src/components/
  Footer         Box, Container, IconButton, Link, Stack, Text, useColorModeValue
  NavLinkButton  Chakra Button
  UserMenu       Avatar, Menu, MenuButton, MenuItem, MenuList

This is the surface every reader sees on every route, so it is also where a lot of already-filed symptoms come from:

1. COLOUR PAIRS THAT ARE HALF LEGACY. Footer.tsx:
     useColorModeValue('gray.50',   'bg.secondary')
     useColorModeValue('gray.700',  'text.secondary')
     useColorModeValue('gray.700',  'text.secondary')
     useColorModeValue('black',     'text.primary')
   Light takes Chakra's stock grey ramp, dark takes Horizon roles - and the dark
   half uses the legacy alias names from the compatibility bridge, not the v2
   roles they forward to. So the footer is the one surface where light mode is
   not on the token system at all, and where removing the bridge (release M8)
   would break it.

2. NO HEADER OR FOOTER LANDMARK. Neither element is rendered as <header> or
   <footer> - measured: an element inside the navbar has no 'header' ancestor.
   There are two <nav> elements inside Navbar and nothing else.

3. horizon-blog-uix.11's mobile hamburger wearing the primary CTA fill is here,
   not in a page.

Doing this closes the migration honestly: right now 'every page migrated' is true and still leaves the most-seen component in the app on the old system.
close_reason:
The shell is on the design system. Every claim below was measured in a browser against the production build.

WHAT MOVED
  AppLayout      -> AppFrame, with real header/main/footer landmarks
  Navbar         -> ContentContainer, NavItem, IconButton, Button, ActionLink,
                    ThemeToggle, Reveal, and componentTokens.header
  Footer         -> ContentContainer, Stack, Text, ActionLink, semantic tokens
  UserMenu       -> control sizing and surface tokens. Chakra Menu stays: the
                    system has no menu, and a popup with roving focus and
                    typeahead is not a thing to reimplement in a shell file.
  NavLinkButton  -> deleted; NavItem replaces it

componentTokens.header had existed since the system was built and nothing ever read it. So had AppFrame, NavItem and ThemeToggle - the shell components were all there, just never wired up.

SEVEN DEFECTS FIXED, verified at 375 and 1440 in both themes:

1. No landmarks. Now header, main with id main-content and tabindex -1, footer, and the AppFrame skip link resolving to that id at z-index 1600 - above the sticky bar it skips past.
2. The navigation never said where you were. NavItem renders React Router NavLink, so the router writes aria-current itself: on /blog exactly one item carries it. The old NavLinkButton marked nothing.
3. Sign in was a button inside an anchor - two tab stops for one destination, and invalid HTML. It is ActionLink at primary weight now; a query for an anchor containing a button returns nothing.
4. A signed-out reader could not switch to dark at all. The toggle lived inside UserMenu, which only renders for a signed-in user. Verified signed out: light to dark, body/header/footer all follow, footer link contrast 8.05:1.
5. The footer social icons went nowhere - three IconButtons with a label and no href. They are links to the real profiles now. There is deliberately no X/Twitter entry: no account for it exists anywhere in the site's own data.
6. The footer navigated with a plain href, a full document load between two pages of one site. Routed now.
7. The hamburger said Open Menu while open, carried no aria-expanded, and left the menu open after navigating. Measured: 44x44, transparent fill rather than the primary CTA fill of horizon-blog-uix.11, label switching Open/Close, aria-expanded false-true-false, aria-controls wired, and a link press both navigates and closes.

THE LIGHT-MODE TOKEN HOLE IS CLOSED. The footer's four useColorModeValue pairs took Chakra's stock grey ramp in light and Horizon roles in dark - and the dark half named legacy aliases from the compatibility bridge, so this file would have broken when M8 removes it. Semantic tokens carry both themes, so the pairs are gone rather than corrected.

TARGETS. The header is now clean of sub-44px controls. Footer links take the system floor with the same inline padding NavItem uses, so a short word like Blog is not a 35px-wide target.

VISUAL CHANGE WORTH KNOWING: the bar no longer uses the Glassmorphism blur. The header token is bg.surface, an opaque fill, which is what the system specifies - so the frosted effect is gone in favour of the system's own surface. It would need a translucent header token to come back, and the system does not have one.

LEDGER: the four surviving app-shell rows move from adapt to migrated, the NavLinkButton row is gone, and every derived count was recomputed from the rows rather than edited by hand - 127 files, 127 rows, 88 migrated, 13 adapt.

Gate: 1501 tests passed across 149 files (4 new), with tsc, lint, format, coverage:design-system and build all exit 0.

title: No systemic guard against an unbreakable string, so long text bursts the layout
description:
Answer to 'do we control this': no. It is patched component by component, each time someone trips over it.

MECHANISM, measured:
Chakra's reset leaves every element at overflow-wrap: break-word. That property breaks a long word onto the next line but does NOT reduce the element's min-content width - only overflow-wrap: anywhere (or word-break: break-word) does. Flex and grid children default to min-width: auto, which floors them at min-content. So one unbreakable token forces its box to the token's full width, and whatever sits above either clips it or lets the page scroll.

The design system already knows this, one case at a time: 20 files carry an ad-hoc minWidth: 0, and ActionLink is the only place using the correct overflowWrap: anywhere - added after a 672px project URL was clipped inside a 343px CV card. Nothing generalises it.

TWO FAILURE MODES, both measured at 375 with a 56-character unbroken string:

  /cv    h1 renders 1224px inside a 293px column. article.cv-document has
         overflow-x: hidden, scrollWidth 1248 vs clientWidth 341.
         -> text is silently truncated and unreachable. Page does not scroll,
            so nothing tells the reader anything is missing.

  /login same growth, nothing clips: the page itself goes 375 -> 709px.
         -> whole layout scrolls sideways.

  gallery every text run replaced with the token: 197 boxes clip their text
         unreachably, 113 become scrollable.

IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION: volume of text is NOT the problem. A 170-character
multi-word title wraps correctly on every page tested - measured growth 0.
Only unbreakable strings break the layout: URLs, code identifiers, hashes,
Vietnamese or German written without spaces. That changes the fix - it is a
wrapping guard, not a truncation or a clamp.

Pages with fixed editorial copy (/about, /contact, 404) survive today only
because their copy is short and controlled. Every surface carrying
user-authored text - post and Series titles, author names, tags, comments - has
the same missing guard, and those could not be retested here because the LAN
backend is unreachable.

PROPOSED CONTROL (not just a fix):
 1. Put the guard in the theme's global styles rather than in components, so it
    cannot be forgotten by the next component.
 2. Unit-test the theme for it, so the guard cannot be removed silently.
 3. Keep the browser stress probe as a manual gate for the layout half, which
    no unit test in this repo can reach - the suite has no layout engine.
close_reason:
Guard shipped in the theme's global styles, with a unit test, and verified against the production build in a browser that paints.

WHAT SHIPPED - src/theme/horizon.ts, styles.global:
  '*'            overflowWrap: 'anywhere'
  'pre, pre *'   overflowWrap: 'normal'

Chakra's reset is ':where(*) { overflow-wrap: break-word }' - zero specificity, so a plain '*' rule beats it. Confirmed: the sign-in heading computes 'anywhere', a 'pre' computes 'normal'.

THE min-width HAMMER WAS DROPPED, because it was measured and it does nothing. On /login at 375 with a 56-character token:
  no guard                 page 709px, h1 1042px
  min-width: 0 alone       page 709px, h1 1042px   <- changes nothing
  overflow-wrap: anywhere  page 375px, h1  343px   <- the whole fix
  both together            page 375px, h1  343px
Only 'anywhere' also shrinks min-content, which is the floor a flex child's 'min-width: auto' sits on. The twenty components carrying a hand-placed minWidth: 0 were treating a symptom, and the global one-liner would have been a large blast radius for no effect.

BOTH MEASURED FAILURES ARE GONE, on the real build at 375:
  /login   page 375 -> 375 (grew 0), h1 1042px -> 343px
  /cv      h1 1224px -> 293px; article.cv-document scrollWidth 1248 vs
           clientWidth 341 -> 341 vs 341, so the name is no longer cut off

NO COLLATERAL DAMAGE, measured rather than eyeballed. Comparing every text block's height with the guard against Chakra's old value, on real content:
  /cv     101 blocks, exactly 1 changed - the publication URL
          vap.ac.vn/Portals/0/TuyenTap/... went 20px (one clipped line) to
          60px (three wrapped lines). That is the defect, not a regression.
  /about   55 blocks, 0 changed.
Ordinary words wrap exactly as before; only strings with nowhere to break behave differently.

THE CODE EXCEPTION IS DELIBERATE. A listing is read by line and a token split mid-word is a corrupted token, so 'pre' keeps 'normal' and scrolls - which is also what horizon-blog-uix.10 wants to give a scroll affordance to. Inline 'code' inside a sentence is deliberately NOT excepted: it wraps with the prose, or one long identifier bursts the article at 375.

RESIDUAL, split out as its own issue: an A/B on the component gallery under the same token shows boxes that still lose text going 88 -> 37. The 118 boxes truncating by design (white-space: nowrap, text-overflow: ellipsis) are untouched, correctly. The remaining 37 are component-level and need individual attention.

Gate: 1497 tests passed (148 files), tsc, lint, format and coverage:design-system all exit 0.

title: Section labels are eyebrow paragraphs, so pages have no usable outline
description:
Found in a page-by-page sweep of the static routes at 1440 and 375, light and dark. The visible heading of a section is an Eyebrow rendered as

at 13px uppercase, not an

. The measured outlines: /cv H1, H3 x8 - zero h2 on the page /about H1, H3,H3,H3, H2, H3x4, H2, H3x4, H2 /contact H1, H3,H3,H3, H2, H3,H3,H3 Two defects, one cause: 1. /cv has no h2 at all. 'Summary', 'Experience', 'Education' are

at 13px/500. A reader navigating by heading gets a name and then eight sibling h3 job titles with nothing grouping them. 2. On /about and /contact the h2 that does exist sits AFTER the h3 cards it should introduce - the first three cards on both pages have no section heading above them at all. The outline is not just flat, it is out of order. Both pages also pass the probe on contrast, overflow and images in both themes, so this is structure only - nothing looks wrong on screen, which is exactly why it survived the migration. Fix direction: the section label and the Eyebrow are two different jobs. Where an Eyebrow names a section, the accessible name should be an h2 (visually still the eyebrow); where it is decoration above a heading that already exists, it stays a

. Decide per section rather than globally.
close_reason:
Fixed, and it needed a new component rather than a relabelling.

THE DIAGNOSIS CHANGED ON CLOSER LOOK. The issue said /about and /contact put their h2 after the h3 cards it should introduce. They do not. Both pages have correct h2s in every labelled section; what they had was a group of h3 cards in the hero with no h2 anywhere above them - About's three editorial tracks under the kicker "Editorial track", and Contact's three channel cards under no label at all. /cv was as described: five section labels rendered as 13px paragraphs, so the page had one h1 and eight sibling h3s and nothing in between.

WHY NOT JUST PROMOTE THE EYEBROW. `Eyebrow`'s own type refuses `as="h2"`, and its doc comment says why: an eyebrow repeats or categorises the heading below it, so putting it in the outline gives every section two entries. That rule is right, and these labels are the other case - the only name a group has, with no heading under them. The system had no way to say that, which is the actual gap this issue exposed.

So `SectionLabel` was added: a real heading at the size of a kicker. Visually identical to `Eyebrow` by construction, and verified so in a browser - both compute 13px/500, 0.65px tracking, uppercase, text.muted, no margins, 20px tall, differing only in tag. Promoting a label changes the outline and nothing on screen.

MEASURED OUTLINES, at 1440 and again at 375:

  /cv       H1,H2,H2,H2,H3,H3,H3,H3,H2,H3,H3,H3,H2,H3
            h2s: Summary, Core Stack, Experience, Personal Projects, Education
            was: H1 then H3 x8, zero h2
  /about    H1,H2,H3,H3,H3,H2,H3,H3,H3,H3,H2,H3,H3,H3,H3,H2
            h2s: Editorial track, Signals, Why Horizon stays open, Tran Tuan Canh
  /contact  H1,H2,H3,H3,H3,H2,H3,H3,H3
            h2s: Ways to reach me, A few helpful reasons to reach out

Zero level skips on all three, at both widths, with no horizontal overflow. Contact's label is new text - "Ways to reach me" - because that group had no name at all to promote; the other six are the existing words, unchanged.

Covered by tests: SectionLabel is a heading and h2 by default, its class matches Eyebrow's exactly, and Eyebrow still renders a p. It is in the gallery registry beside Eyebrow, deliberately, because that is where the distinction between the two is easiest to miss.

SEPARATE FINDING, raised as horizon-blog-g1h: registering it in the gallery did not move the coverage audit's count, which is how a blind spot in that audit came to light - it skips every forwardRef component, 38 of them.

Gate: 1504 tests (150 files), tsc, lint, format, coverage:design-system and build all exit 0.

title: Article code blocks use a theme-unaware One Dark syntax palette
description:
Split out of horizon-blog-uix.8, which is otherwise done. BLOCKED on two owner decisions.

CodeMirror's One Dark highlight colours are hardcoded and do not respond to the light theme. Measured on /blog/pUxyH8AUZh at 1440 in light, against bg.code rgb(237,241,250): ALL NINE syntax colours fail the 4.5:1 floor.

  1.53:1  rgb(229,192,123)  numbers        (4 spans)
  1.78:1  rgb(152,195,121)  strings        (1)
  1.88:1  rgb(171,178,191)  punctuation    (16)
  2.09:1  rgb(86,182,194)   operators      (35)
  2.09:1  rgb(97,175,239)   functions      (2)
  2.18:1  rgb(209,154,102)  constants      (5)
  ... 9 of 9 below 4.5:1

Unblocking needs the owner to decide:
  (a) declare @codemirror/language and @lezer/highlight as direct dependencies - they resolve to MODULE_NOT_FOUND under Yarn PnP today, so no highlight style can be registered at all; and
  (b) approve ~8 paired code.syntax.* semantic tokens (keyword, string, number, comment, function, type, operator, invalid). The Signal baseline approved 19 roles and none of them cover syntax, so these are new approved colour decisions, not derived ones.
notes:
PARTIALLY DONE. The two things this issue was blocked on are both delivered; the wiring that consumes them is not, and that is the whole of what remains.

DONE - dependencies.
@codemirror/language ^6.12.1 and @lezer/highlight ^1.2.3 are direct dependencies now, at the versions the lockfile already resolved transitively. Lockfile regenerated, `yarn install --immutable` clean, and both resolve under PnP (previously MODULE_NOT_FOUND).

DONE - the eight approved token pairs, and they cost no new pigment.
Every value is an approved palette step already used elsewhere, which is what `derived` means in semantic.ts. Measured against bg.code, light and dark:

  keyword   cobalt.800 / cobalt.300     6.91 / 9.67
  function  cobalt.600 / cobalt.400     5.34 / 7.86
  type      lime.800   / lime.300      10.94 / 13.96
  string    success.600/ success.300    5.72 / 10.81
  number    warning.600/ warning.300    5.59 / 11.35
  operator  mist.700   / night.200      5.53 / 8.93
  comment   mist.600   / night.300      4.77 / 6.57
  invalid   danger.600 / danger.300     5.74 / 8.77

Floor 4.77:1, ceiling 13.96:1. The only two approved steps that could not clear 4.5 on bg.code (mist.500 at 3.03, night.400 at 4.38) are simply unused. `code` was added to the token families the test allows, because a family names what a colour is for and code is a kind of content, not a page. tokens.json regenerated: 50 semantic roles.

NOT DONE - making Crepe use them.
`crepe.syntax.ts` builds a HighlightStyle naming those tokens through Chakra's CSS variables, so one static extension serves both themes. CodeMirror accepts it and injects its stylesheet - eight rules naming --chakra-colors-code-syntax-* are in the document, and the variables resolve (keyword computes #2648B6). But no span ever receives their classes. Every listing still renders in One Dark and still fails the floor in light, exactly as before.

Three routes measured, all wrong:
  extensions, no precedence   One Dark wins the tag
  theme, as an array          Crepe merges with lodash defaultsDeep, which walks
                              arrays element by element: our entry landed at
                              index 0 and One Dark's highlight style survived at
                              index 1 - the listing came out with our background
                              and One Dark's colours
  theme, as a Prec object     stylesheet injected, highlighter never reaches the
                              facet; the listing fell through to basicSetup's

title: Contact has no entry motion at all, and About's is too small to read
description:
Two different problems behind the same symptom.

/contact - NO MOTION AT ALL.
ContactPage imports neither Reveal nor Stagger (grep count: 0). Measured at 1440: all six cards have no animated ancestor anywhere up the tree, and the card itself computes transition-duration 0s. Home, /blog and /about all use Stagger or Reveal, so Contact is the page that was missed - every other surface in the system enters, this one is just suddenly there.

/about - MOTION EXISTS, BUT BARELY REGISTERS, AND IS INCONSISTENT.
All eight cards do animate; my first pass said otherwise because it only looked at the card's immediate parent, and three of them are revealed further up. Corrected measurements:
  about-signals  4 cards, animated ancestor at depth 1 - per card, via Stagger
  about-founder  1 card,  depth 1
  about-approach 3 cards, depth 4 - the whole section enters as ONE block
So two different granularities on one page: some cards arrive one after another, others arrive together, with nothing in the content to justify the difference.

And the gesture itself is small: Reveal is a fade plus at most 8px of upward travel over 320ms (the 'enter' token). On a card around 200px tall, 8px of travel is close to invisible - which is very likely why it reads as 'no animation' even where it is working.

Worth settling as one decision rather than three patches:
  1. Does Contact enter like every other page? (almost certainly yes)
  2. Is a section revealed as a block ever right, or should cards always stagger?
  3. Is 8px the intended travel, or a placeholder nobody revisited? It is the
     one number that decides whether any of this is perceptible.

Separately worth ruling out on the reporter's machine: macOS System Settings > Accessibility > Display > Reduce motion collapses every duration to zero by design, and would make even a corrected animation invisible.
close_reason:
Entry motion is on every page now, per card, and far enough to see.

THE TRAVEL. `transform.revealDistance` 8px -> 14px. 8px on a card 200px tall is close to invisible, which is why the entry was reported as "no animation at all" on pages where it was working correctly. The fade still does most of the work and reduced motion still takes the travel to zero.

CONTACT had no entry motion at all - it imported neither Reveal nor Stagger, while Home, /blog and /about all did. Both card groups are staggered now. Measured at 1440: 6 of 6 cards carry their own animated wrapper at depth 1, where before none carried one at any depth. The three above the fold have finished; the fourth is still at opacity 0 waiting for its turn, which is `inView` behaving correctly.

ABOUT had two granularities on one page. The four signal cards and the founder note staggered per card; the three approach cards rode the section's single Reveal and arrived as one block - nothing in the content justified the difference. Measured after: all eight cards at depth 1 with translateY(14px), where the approach three were previously at depth 4.

A correction to this issue's own first report: it said the approach cards did not animate. They did - the measurement had only looked at each card's immediate parent, and their wrapper was three levels further up. The defect was the granularity, not the absence.

title: 37 components still lose text to an unbreakable string
description:
Residual from horizon-blog-aun, which fixed the systemic half.

The global overflow-wrap guard took the gallery's text-losing boxes from 88 to 37 under a 56-character unbreakable token at 375 (A/B on one page, one run, same token). The 118 boxes that truncate by design - white-space: nowrap or text-overflow: ellipsis - are deliberately untouched by it, since no wrapping rule can help a line that refuses to wrap.

The 37 that remain are not reachable by a wrapping rule either. Sampled: article elements at scrollWidth 482 vs clientWidth 298, already computing overflow-wrap: anywhere with white-space: normal - so the width is being set by a descendant (a fixed-width child, a nested grid track, or a nowrap child inside a wrapping box), not by the text itself.

Each needs looking at on its own terms, and the answer will differ: some should shrink, some should scroll, and some are metadata that is genuinely better truncated with an ellipsis and a title.

Reproduce: serve the build, open /ui-kit.html at 375, replace the text of every h1-h6/a/p/span/li with a long unbreakable token, then count elements where overflow-x is hidden and scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth, excluding pre, nowrap, ellipsis and line-clamp. The probe used is in the session scratchpad as stress.js.

Worth pairing with the surfaces carrying user-authored text - post and Series titles, author names, tags, comments - which could not be retested when this was found because the LAN backend was unreachable.
notes:
Wave 3, 2026-09-15. 30 -> 10 boxes (baseline measured 30 on this build, not the 37 in the description - same probe method, later snapshot).

CORRECTION to this bead's premise: it is not 37 components each needing its own answer. The 30 instances came from 6 root causes counted repeatedly: Chip x14, StatusBadge x6, AuthorIdentity initials x6, DataTable thead x1, DiagramFrame header x2, ResponsiveImage retry x1. Fixing two components (Chip, StatusBadge) plus two wrappers missing min-width:0 closed 20 of them.

The 10 that remain are deliberate. Seven are probe false positives: authorInitials() is data-bounded to 2 characters so the 56-char token cannot occur there, and DataTable's thead is position:absolute + clip:rect(0 0 0 0), the standard visually-hidden pattern. The probe's exclusion list should grow to cover data-bounded text and the visually-hidden clip pattern alongside nowrap/ellipsis/line-clamp.

Three need an owner call, documented in the wave-3 report: DiagramFrame's space-between header row (wrap to two lines vs truncate the caption) and ResponsiveImage's retry button (7px from a real label - truncating a retry CTA is bad, letting it wrap changes Button globally).

title: A hung network leaves pages loading forever with no timeout and no way out
description:
Observed while auditing with the LAN backend unreachable (host drops packets rather than refusing, so sockets hang instead of failing).

Home at 1440: the signature skeleton and the Series shelf skeletons were still showing 28 seconds after load, with no error state, no retry and no explanation. Three requests were still pending - GET /series, GET /posts/summaries, POST /auth/refresh - none had settled.

The error paths themselves are correct: usePublicSeriesList catches, sets an error and clears loading, and HomePage has an ErrorState with a RetryAction. They are simply never reached, because nothing caps how long a request may take. The reader is left with a page that looks like it is about to finish, forever.

Fix direction: an AbortController deadline in the api service, so a request that has not answered within a sensible budget rejects like any other failure and the existing error and retry states do their job. One place, not per hook.

Related: horizon-blog-uix.12 notes /auth/refresh 401s on every anonymous load - a request that should not be made at all here is one of the three left hanging.

title: Standalone call-to-action links are 26px tall, under the system's own 44px floor
description:
Measured on every static route at 1440 and 375.

ActionLink at its default text weight is used as a standalone call to action all over the site, and it renders 26px tall - the line box, with no control padding. ActionLink's own source says 'md is the 44x44 touch target of the accessibility floor', and applies that sizing only at button weight.

Counts per page (height 26px in every case):
  /about     5  Read the blog, Get in touch, View CV, GitHub, LinkedIn
  /contact   4  Email directly, Call instead, and the two contact values
  404        3  Go home, Browse blogs, All series
  /          2  Create an account, View all series
  /login     1  Forgot password?
  /cv        1  Contact  (plus Export PDF at 40px, also short)

At 375 several stretch to full width (293-343px) but stay 26px tall, so the target is wide and thin - the dimension a thumb actually misses.

This clears WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 (24x24 minimum) but fails the 44px floor the design system states for itself, which is the standard that should apply.

Not a blanket fix: an inline link inside a paragraph is text and must stay text. This is specifically about links that stand alone as the action of a section or a card.

title: Readers cannot copy code from an article
description:
PRODUCT CALL - needs the owner's decision, not a bug fix on sight.

src/components/editor/crepe-theme.css:592

  .crepe-editor-wrapper[data-readonly='true'] .milkdown-code-block .tools { display: none }

The reading surface hides the code block's tools row, which is where Crepe's Copy button lives. The very next rule brings it back for blocks that contain a mermaid preview, so a reader can copy a diagram's source but not a shell command or a Python snippet - the blocks people actually copy.

Hiding the row is defensible: it also carries the language picker and the preview toggle, which are authoring controls and have no business on a published article. The question is whether Copy is an authoring control or a reading one. If it is a reading one, the fix is to show that one button rather than the row.

Raised by the P1 fix agent while working horizon-blog-uix.8; deliberately not decided by an agent.
close_reason:
A reader can copy code again, and only the Copy button came back.

crepe-theme.css hid the whole tools row on a reading surface, which took the Copy button with it - and the rule below it brought the row back for mermaid blocks, so a reader could copy the source of a diagram but not a shell command or a Python snippet. Copy is a reading control: it takes the listing away with you and changes nothing in the document.

The row's three children, read off the rendered DOM rather than guessed: `.language-button`, the `.language-picker` popup it opens, and `.tools-button-group` holding Copy. The first two restate and change what language a published listing is written in, which is the author's decision and already made. Those two are hidden; the button group stays. My first attempt hid `input` instead, which missed entirely - the picker is a button.

Measured on a reading surface over a Python listing:
  .language-button    display none
  .language-picker    display none
  .tools-button-group visible, containing Copy
  .tools              justify-content flex-end, so the buttons sit right on
                      their own once the picker is gone

Crepe keeps those buttons at opacity 0 until the block is hovered, which is right for a pointer and unreachable without one, so a `:focus-visible` rule reveals them for a keyboard reader too.

title: Non-UI findings from the real-data sweep
description: Four things the sweep found that are wrong but are not UI defects. (a) /auth/refresh fires on every anonymous page load and always 401s - localStorage holds no token and document.cookie is empty, yet the app spends a round trip during first paint and logs 401 to every visitor's console. (b) Backend excerpt data is polluted: of 48 posts from /posts/summaries, 12 excerpts begin with a literal '1.00 ' and 15 contain raw markdown that renders verbatim on cards - post 84's excerpt has a title and the word 'cover' concatenated into it. The data is wrong at source, and the frontend also does not strip markdown from excerpts. (c) /cv imports Public Sans from Google at runtime (cv-fonts.css:1) - a third-party render-blocking @import on one route, while the rest of the app self-hosts Be Vietnam Pro. (d) A 144x108 thumbnail's srcset correctly offers a 19KB w320.webp, but the src fallback points at the original PNG: 2,165,498 bytes, 11.8s.

title: Wide article content has no scroll affordance at 375
description: Tables in an article are table-layout: fixed with clientWidth 279 while their columns sum to 320 (scrollWidth 321) - the row's right edge sits at 369 against a table edge of 327. The content is reachable, because the table is its own overflow-x scroller, but there is no scrollbar and no fade, so '/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg' simply looks cut off. The .table-wrapper around it is overflow: visible and does not scroll. Fenced code compounds it: 19px at 1440 and 18px at 375 against 16px prose, in bare monospace because no DS mono token reaches it, so at 375 a 239px scroller holds 712px of content.
acceptance_criteria: Wide content in an article announces that it scrolls, at both widths, and code sits at or below the prose size rather than above it.

title: Draft recovery is written but never read back
description: Found during release M6. src/features/editor/hooks/useAutoSave.ts writes a full copy of the draft to localStorage under blog_draft_backup on every keystroke, and removes it on a successful save - but no code path ever reads it back. Verified: there is no getItem for that key anywhere in src. So the recovery half of draft recovery has never existed; only the cost of writing it does. The design system has draftRecovery() and WorkspaceShell has a banner slot, so the UI side is ready. M6 deliberately did not wire it: letting a local copy overwrite server content is new behaviour, not a migration, and it needs a product decision first.
acceptance_criteria: Decide the rule before writing code: when is a local backup offered, who wins when local and server disagree, does the author see what differs before choosing, and what happens to the backup if they decline. Then either wire draftRecovery() to that rule, or delete the setItem so the editor stops writing article content to localStorage that nothing will ever use.

title: Signal behavioral design system v1
description:
Signal is Horizon Blog's shared product language for public and protected surfaces. It combines editorial clarity, soft tactile depth, purposeful motion, real-content resilience, and equal light/dark quality. This decision records the behavioral layer learned from R1 so later releases do not regress into flat static layouts or duplicate one rounded card treatment everywhere.

The core visual tokens remain Be Vietnam Pro, cobalt actions, restrained lime emphasis, semantic surfaces, soft radii, and layered editorial shadows. Future work should evolve component behavior and state contracts before adding more palette tokens.
design:
## Product character

- Personal technical blog: thoughtful, lively, editorial, tactile, and reader-first.
- Minimal means clear hierarchy and controlled chrome; it does not mean flat or motionless.
- Reading surfaces remain stable. Discovery surfaces may use richer depth, reveal, pointer, hover, and navigation feedback.

## Component contract

Every reusable interactive component defines:

1. Semantic role and content hierarchy.
2. Surface depth at rest and on interaction.
3. Hover, press, keyboard focus, touch, entry/reveal, and navigation feedback.
4. Reduced-motion alternative that preserves clear state feedback.
5. Loading, ready, empty, no-media, error, and retry states where data or media is involved.
6. Desktop, intermediate, and mobile behavior, including long real titles and excerpts.
7. Light and dark presentation with semantic tokens.

Shared primitives may standardize behavior such as InteractiveSurface, MediaFrame, HorizontalRail, PageLoading, metadata, and section headings. Domain components keep distinct identities: Signature, StoryCard, SeriesCard, reader context, auth panel, and analytics panel must not collapse into one universal card.

## R1 evidence carried forward

- Prototype screenshots alone did not expose real-data failures; use production-shaped content before acceptance.
- Series is the reference interaction quality: distinct book identity, pagination, drag, snap, overlay controls, keyboard support, retained data during page loading, error retry, mobile peek, and reduced motion.
- Media is a first-class state machine: loading, fade-in ready, title fallback when absent, error, and retry.
- Navigation uses balanced desktop zones and a detached mobile panel instead of expanding the header.
- Visual QA is separate from tests and HTTP health. Validate desktop/mobile, light/dark, mouse/keyboard/touch, normal/reduced motion, long content, and failed media.

## Release guidance

- R2: founder/About reveals and tactile links; CV and Contact remain calm and readable.
- R3: image-first Blog discovery, responsive search/filter/pagination transitions, personal scan-first Author archive, and Series book/connector language.
- R4: consolidate shared motion and add reader progress, TOC, copy, reaction, media, and route feedback while prose remains stable.
- R5: restrained branded auth loading and form feedback.
- R6: motion communicates autosave, upload, publish, schedule, permissions, charts, and table state rather than decoration.
acceptance_criteria: Be Vietnam Pro, cobalt action roles, restrained lime accents, semantic light and dark surfaces, and layered editorial shadows are the baseline. Every release defines interaction, async and media states, responsive behavior, accessibility, reduced motion, and a real-data visual validation matrix before acceptance.
notes:
1. Be Vietnam Pro, cobalt action roles, restrained lime accents, semantic light/dark surfaces, and layered editorial shadows are treated as the current Signal baseline.
2. Each release specifies component anatomy, real-data constraints, responsive behavior, interaction states, async/media states, accessibility, and reduced-motion behavior before implementation.
3. Visual acceptance covers desktop and mobile, light and dark, mouse and keyboard, touch where relevant, normal and reduced motion, long content, empty/error states, and media failure.
4. Shared behavioral primitives are reused without turning Signature, writing, Series, reader, auth, and analytics surfaces into one universal card.
5. R3 applies the R1 lessons to real Blog, Author, and Series services without changing API, authorization, route, or data contracts.

design:
## R3.2 design contract

- Public Series keeps the book/reading-thread identity established on Home. Series cards must remain visually distinct from blog cards.
- The Series index uses a clear editorial introduction, one leading Series when data supports it, and a responsive discovery layout. Avoid course, progress, completion, and dashboard language.
- Series detail uses a loose editorial header and ordered parts with visible numbering and connectors. Hover and keyboard focus emphasize the active part and outgoing connector; touch receives clear press feedback.
- Preserve existing public Series service ordering and published-only rules. Loading, empty, error, retry, not-found, and partial data states are first-class and must not block unrelated blog content.
- Reuse behavioral primitives from R1 where appropriate: tactile surface depth, book cover layers, media and async state feedback, reduced motion, semantic light/dark tokens, and responsive mobile interaction.
- Validate desktop/mobile, light/dark, mouse/keyboard/touch, normal/reduced motion, zero/one/many parts, long titles/descriptions, pagination if returned by the service, and API failure with production-shaped data.

## R3.1 design contract

- Blog discovery is tighter than Home but retains tactile depth and perceptible interaction.
- Preserve real search, filters, query state, pagination, author navigation, public metadata meaning, and Series shelf visibility rules.
- Use image-first editorial cards with a clear hierarchy among leading story and standard results. Do not repeat one identical rounded card treatment.
- Reuse the Home media state contract: loading, ready fade-in, title fallback for no media, error, and retry. Clean excerpts before display and test long Vietnamese and English content.
- Search, filter chips, result changes, pagination, card hover/press/focus, CTA arrows, and entry reveal must have purposeful feedback. Touch must not depend on hover. Reduced motion removes translation while retaining color, border, or shadow feedback.
- Author archive remains personal and scan-first: designed identity rail, chronological writing rows, subtle ambient depth, clear pagination, no owner controls or fabricated public fields.
- Validate desktop/mobile, light/dark, mouse/keyboard/touch, normal/reduced motion, empty/search-empty/error/retry, long content, and failed media using production-shaped data.

# Horizon redesign: approved design tokens v0.2

Decision date: 2026-09-05.
Scope: Horizon Blog UI/UX redesign, frontend project /Users/trantuancanh/Personal/work/horizon-blog/horizon-blog.
Status: User approved recording this direction and all tokens in Beads after viewing the revised light/dark mockups. This is a design baseline; not implemented in production, not a complete component design system, and not a claim that all product flows have been designed or tested.

## Approved direction and durable corrections
- Selected reference: the SECOND displayed image of the fresh Terra / Signal / Nocturne ideation set: SIGNAL, cobalt with restrained lime.
- User rejected prior exploration for keeping old design tokens; do not treat the old slate-blue palette or old geometry/font rules as fixed constraints for this authorized redesign.
- User then said all directions were too rigid/lifeless and explicitly required dark mode.
- Approved evolution: retain Signal identity, soften typography and shapes, introduce restrained layered surfaces and meaningful tactile editorial illustration.
- Preserve personal technical-blog purpose and actual capabilities. Do not turn public reading into a dashboard, course system or marketing feature inventory.
- Same layout, hierarchy and core content in light and dark modes. Dark mode is designed with semantic roles, not mechanical inversion.
- Exact token values below are authoritative for implementation; generated raster images are visual references and are not pixel-accurate token or font specifications.
- Semantic token names may stay stable while their values and usage change. A redesign must materially reconsider palette, type, geometry, spacing, depth, illustration and motion, rather than just move sections.
- Motion communicates interaction/state; no continuous distracting motion in article prose. Liveliness should come from illustration, meaningful emphasis, soft interaction feedback and spacing.
